headline: High: agentic-flow can modify git and use MCP while the paired content-writing agent has broad egress, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so its outputs may be bridged into other tools or agents; agent_b has broad network egress and could consume forwarded content. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs untrusted text into an MCP-backed workflow that agent_b reads, injection becomes actionable.
IF the orchestrator forwards agent_a stdout to agent_b without provenance filtering, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from agent_a outputs to agent_b inputs.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Require a human review step before agent_b consumes agent_a text.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted commands only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets (Ed25519 signatures), while agent_b has broad network egress. Even without a shared workspace explicitly documented, forwarding agent_a artifacts to agent_b could leak sensitive material; the pairwise path is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are passed to agent_b for summarization or rewriting, sensitive repository data can leave the local boundary.
IF agent_b is allowed to transmit its context to external services, leaked prompts or code may exfiltrate.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets-bearing files from agent_a to agent_b.
Mask signatures and repository metadata before any transfer.
Constrain agent_b to local-only operation for sensitive tasks.
Review outbound destinations for agent_b.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent handoffs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b's write surface is not documented, so direct conflict is uncertain. Because uncertainty must escalate, the overlapping mutable git/workflow path is treated as a real coordination risk rather than none.
conditions: IF agent_b also writes to the same repository or workspace, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF agent_a and agent_b operate on the same git branch without locking, state corruption becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or worktrees.
Serialize write operations with a lock file.
Keep agent_b read-only unless explicitly needed.
Snapshot the repo before agent_a mutates it.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and modify repository artifacts, and agent_b is a content-writing agent that may render or reuse those outputs. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so agent_a mistakes can cascade into agent_b-produced deliverables; the pathway exists even though downstream action authority is not explicit.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source text without verification, errors propagate into final content.
IF agent_a produces incorrect repository facts that agent_b republishes, the mistake becomes user-visible.
mitigations: Require citation or diff checks before agent_b reuse.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Limit agent_b to rewriting only, not factual synthesis.
Flag low-confidence outputs from agent_a.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is open-source and handles repository metadata plus signatures; agent_b is also open-source but its compliance posture is largely undocumented. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is shown, so only a small compliance gap is plausible, and the other agent is not cited beyond its open network posture because no residency data exists.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a's repository workflow, retention and handling must be reviewed.
IF agent_b is used in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, its undocumented handling becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent's workflow.
Document retention for repository metadata and prompts.
Review outbound network destinations before use.
Keep signatures and secrets out of shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment.
